anchors.paper_title: 2021 BEETL Competition: Advancing Transfer Learning for Subject Independence & Heterogenous EEG Data Sets
anchors.reason: The BEETL 2021 competition paper describes the competition and its datasets, including the motor imagery task data; its authors match the dataset's author list.

metadata.methods_description: EEG was acquired at 200 Hz from 32 channels placed around the motor cortex (standard 1005 montage) with online bandpass filtering (1-100 Hz). Data were bandpass filtered in the frequency domain (1-100 Hz) and segmented into 4-second trials. Visual cues indicated four motor imagery classes, and evaluation used block-wise 5-fold cross-validation with cross-subject and cross-dataset assessment.

citation_details.title: Benchmarking brain–computer interface algorithms: Riemannian approaches vs convolutional neural networks
citation_details.author: Manuel Eder, Jiachen Xu, Moritz Grosse‐Wentrup
citation_details.abstract: Abstract Objective. To date, a comprehensive comparison of Riemannian decoding methods with deep convolutional neural networks for EEG-based brain–computer interfaces remains absent from published work. We address this research gap by using MOABB, The Mother Of All BCI Benchmarks, to compare novel convolutional neural networks to state-of-the-art Riemannian approaches across a broad range of EEG datasets, including motor imagery, P300, and steady-state visual evoked potentials paradigms. Approach. We systematically evaluated the performance of convolutional neural networks, specifically EEGNet, shallow ConvNet, and deep ConvNet, against well-established Riemannian decoding methods using MOABB processing pipelines. This evaluation included within-session, cross-session, and cross-subject methods, to provide a practical analysis of model effectiveness and to find an overall solution that performs well across different experimental settings.
